grammar.title: An ability or routine has changed
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast verb + ようになる. Use a potential verb for becoming able: 読む → 読めるようになる; する → できるようになる. A new routine can use an ordinary verb: 記録するようになる. Polite past: ～ようになりました.
grammar.explanation: Describe the resulting change, not merely your intention. A recording from last month and a recording from today can provide an observation to compare. The construction itself doesn’t quantify fluency. These community-N4 forms bridge gaps in this course before the N3 purpose contrast. Loss of an action/ability commonly uses ～なくなる; don’t mechanically turn every negative change into ないようになる.
grammar.example: 以前より短い文を速く読めるようになりました。
grammar.translation: I have become able to read short sentences faster than before.

examples.ja: {以前|いぜん}より{短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}を{速|はや}く{読|よ}めるようになりました。
examples.en: I have become able to read short sentences faster than before.

examples.ja: {練習|れんしゅう}の{後|あと}で{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}すようになりました。

examples.ja: {落|お}ち{着|つ}いて{発表|はっぴょう}できるようになりたいです。

grammar.mistake: 読めるようになりたい describes a wish; 読めるようになりました reports a change. Neither tells us that every text is now understood.

grammar.title: Make a conscious effort
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast/ない verb + ようにする. ～ようにしています describes ongoing effort; ～ようにしてください asks someone to take care to do/not do it.
grammar.explanation: Choose a practice behaviour that you can actually carry out. This expresses care or effort and doesn’t promise perfect performance. Compare a chosen effort (確認するようにしています) with an observed new routine (確認するようになりました). Do not confuse the noun-comparison pattern 見本のように with this clause construction.
grammar.example: 発音を確かめるようにしています。
grammar.translation: I make a point of checking my pronunciation.

examples.ja: {発音|はつおん}を{確|たし}かめるようにしています。
examples.en: I make a point of checking my pronunciation.

examples.ja: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は{無理|むり}をしないようにしています。
examples.en: I try not to push myself when tired.

examples.ja: {提出|ていしゅつ}する{前|まえ}に{報告書|ほうこくしょ}を{見直|みなお}すようにしてください。
examples.en: Please make a point of reviewing the report before submitting it.

grammar.mistake: ようにしている is an ongoing effort. It’s not evidence that an action is always carried out successfully.

grammar.title: Act so that a result becomes possible
grammar.formation: Plain nonpast or ない clause + ように + action. Common first clauses have potential/state verbs: 読める、聞こえる、忘れない. Each clause may have its own subject.
grammar.explanation: The first clause presents an ability, state or avoided outcome; the second describes the action aimed at it. ように doesn’t assert that the goal has already been achieved. The subject can change: everyone should be able to read the text, so one writer enlarges it. The pattern here is purpose, not resemblance.
grammar.example: 後ろの人にも見えるように、字を大きくしました。
grammar.translation: I enlarged the writing so that people at the back can also see it.

examples.ja: {後|うし}ろの{人|ひと}にも{見|み}えるように、{字|じ}を{大|おお}きくしました。
examples.en: I enlarged the writing so that people at the back can also see it.

examples.ja: {方法|ほうほう}を{忘|わす}れないように、{手順|てじゅん}を{記録|きろく}しました。
examples.en: I recorded the steps so I would not forget the method.

examples.ja: {短|みじか}い{会話|かいわ}を{聞|き}き{取|と}れるように、{音|おと}を{調整|ちょうせい}しました。
examples.en: I adjusted the sound so that I can catch the short conversation.

grammar.mistake: Do not use 見えるために in this beginner purpose contrast: 見える is the desired perceptual state, so practise 見えるように.

grammar.title: A deliberate goal: ために versus ように
grammar.formation: Purpose: dictionary-form volitional verb + ために; noun + のために. For a desired ability/state or avoided outcome, use plain nonpast/ない + ように. This unit teaches purpose ために; cause ために is deferred to unit 9.
grammar.explanation: ために connects a purposeful action to a deliberate goal, usually with the same actor controlling both. ように typically aims at a state such as being able to hear. These are useful learning tendencies, not a rule that every verb belongs in only one pattern. Read the context. 学ぶために names deliberate study as the goal; 聞き取れるように aims at listening ability. Do not interpret a practice plan as a completed result.
grammar.example: 新しい方法を学ぶために、講座に参加します。
grammar.translation: I’ll attend the course to learn a new method.

examples.ja: {新|あたら}しい{方法|ほうほう}を{学|まな}ぶために、{講座|こうざ}に{参加|さんか}します。
examples.en: I’ll attend the course to learn a new method.

examples.ja: {発表|はっぴょう}のために、{練習|れんしゅう}の{時間|じかん}を{作|つく}りました。
examples.en: I set aside practice time for the presentation.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}が{聞|き}き{取|と}れるように、{短|みじか}く{区切|くぎ}って{聞|き}きます。
examples.en: I listen in short sections so I can catch the explanation.

grammar.mistake: Nouns need の: 発表のために. Distinguish the goal 発表するために from the observed outcome 発表できるようになった.

glosses.meaning: a course; a series of lessons
part of the grammar patterns taught here

exercises.explain: Bao reports 短い文はすらすら読めるようになりました, then says long explanations are still difficult.

exercises.prompt: What does Bao make a point of doing after practice?
options: Watching a course recording before practice
exercises.explain: 練習の後で、記録を見直すようにしています specifies both action and timing.
次の課題は、方法を短く説明することです states the next task.

exercises.context: Report an observed new ability, not a wish or an ongoing effort.
exercises.line: {短|みじか}い{文|ぶん}をすらすら{読|よ}める＿＿。
exercises.explain: ようになりました reports the changed ability; the other endings state an effort or wish.

exercises.context: State a current conscious habit of checking records. Do not report when the habit started.
exercises.line: {記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}す＿＿。
exercises.explain: ようにしています marks ongoing effort. The context asks for that meaning.

exercises.context: Answer Satō-sensei politely: the new habit’s reviewing the method record. Do not change the topic.
exercises.line: {以前|いぜん}と{比|くら}べて、{何|なに}をするようになりましたか。
options: {方法|ほうほう}の{記録|きろく}を{見直|みなお}すようになりました。
{方法|ほうほう}の{説明|せつめい}は{来週|らいしゅう}です。
{記録|きろく}は{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}です。
exercises.explain: The first reply identifies the changed routine. The others give a date or location.

exercises.context: Tell the teacher politely that you try not to push yourself when tired.
exercises.line: {疲|つか}れた{時|とき}は、どうしていますか。
options: {無理|むり}をしないようにしています。
{無理|むり}をするようにしています。
{疲|つか}れるために{練習|れんしゅう}しています。
exercises.explain: The negative しない expresses the intended avoidance. The other replies contradict the specified plan.

exercises.meaning: I make a point of looking over the record after practice.
tiles: {練習|れんしゅう}の{後|あと}で、
exercises.explain: The nonpast clause 見直す precedes ようにしています; 練習の後で gives the timing.

exercises.prompt: Why should the writing be enlarged?
options: So people at the back can see it
exercises.explain: Satō-sensei explicitly says 後ろの人にも見えるように.

exercises.prompt: Why will Bao attend next week’s course?
options: To submit an already completed exam result
exercises.explain: 新しい方法を学ぶために gives a deliberate goal, not a result already achieved.

exercises.context: Practise the purpose construction for a deliberate action: attending a course to learn a method.
exercises.line: {新|あたら}しい{方法|ほうほう}を{学|まな}ぶ＿＿、{講座|こうざ}に{参加|さんか}します。
exercises.explain: Dictionary-form 学ぶ + ために names the goal. のに is a concession and までに a deadline.

exercises.context: Aim for an ability, not a completed result. Complete the sentence about audio adjustment.
exercises.line: {説明|せつめい}が{聞|き}き{取|と}れる＿＿、{音|おと}を{調整|ちょうせい}します。
exercises.explain: 聞き取れるように gives the desired ability. のに gives contrast and ようになった would report a completed change.

exercises.meaning: I’ll display the steps for the presentation.
exercises.explain: A noun purpose uses のために. Displaying the steps is the action serving it.

exercises.prompt: What does the writer prioritise this week?
exercises.explain: 今週は速さより正確さを優先する explicitly states the priority.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

exercises.prompt: Which pair correctly separates a result from a future plan?
options: Can now read short sentences smoothly; will attend a course next week
Will attend a course; already understands every long explanation
Can now read every text; will stop reviewing
exercises.explain: The first paragraph reports a limited achieved change. The final paragraph schedules the course.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

exercises.prompt: What will the writer do on a tired day?
exercises.explain: 疲れた日は休む states the action directly.
exercises.context: Read the diary; choose the statement supported by it.

grammar: ようになる / ようにする
purpose ように / ために
watch.prompt: Optionally use your own short vlog. Save a line describing a change and a line describing a purpose. Mark whether each line reports an outcome or a goal; don’t infer fluency from a goal.
